conversation.content:
Hi there—I’m so glad you’re here.  
My name is Maya, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician; I spend my days supporting new mothers as they navigate the emotional ups and downs that can come after a baby arrives.  

Today I’ll be guiding you through a short questionnaire called the **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale**, or EPDS for short. It’s simply a tool that helps us understand how you’ve been feeling during the past seven days so we can be sure you’re getting the right kind of support.  

Everything you share is confidential, and this is a judgment-free space. There are just ten questions; most moms finish in under five minutes. We’ll go at your pace, and you can pause or ask for clarification any time.  

Whenever you’re ready, we can start with the first question.

---

In the past week, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt difficult?

[slow exhale]  
I guess… I can still laugh, but it feels kind of forced. Like, my sister sent me a funny video yesterday and I chuckled, but then the smile just slid right off. Most of the time nothing feels very funny, so yeah—it’s been difficult.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Not really. I can manage a little laugh here or there, but it doesn’t come easy—most things just don’t feel funny anymore.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really... I used to get excited about little stuff—coffee with a friend, a walk, even just a quiet shower—but now it all feels flat. Sometimes I make plans hoping the spark will come back, but when the time comes I’m just going through the motions.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah... I do that a lot. If the baby’s fussy, I immediately think it’s something I ate or that I’m not soothing him right. Last night he wouldn’t settle, and I kept replaying the day, convinced I must’ve done something wrong. I know it’s probably not all my fault, but the guilt just jumps in before I can stop it.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yeah, pretty much every day. I’ll be feeding the baby and suddenly my heart’s racing about... nothing. Or I’ll imagine him choking in the crib and have to check the monitor five times. There’s no real reason, just this constant worry sitting on my chest.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Sometimes. It’s not like a full panic attack, but a couple of nights I’ve woken up with my heart pounding and this wave of dread, and I can’t even tell you what I’m scared of—just this feeling that something awful is about to happen.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes… most days feel like I’m barely keeping my head above water. I’ll finally get the baby down and see the pile of laundry or the dishes, and it’s like a wave crashes over me—my chest gets tight, I can’t catch my breath, and I think, “I can’t do this.” I usually still push through, but it feels overwhelming more often than not.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yeah, that’s been happening. I’ll lie there after the baby finally settles, exhausted but my mind just spins—worrying I’m not doing enough, replaying every little thing from the day. It takes me forever to fall asleep, and if I wake up to check on him, I can’t drift back off. I end up staring at the ceiling feeling this heavy sadness.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yes... most of the day, most days. It’s like a gray cloud that just hangs there, even when I’m doing “normal” stuff. I’ll be rocking the baby and tears start welling up for no clear reason. I keep thinking I should feel happy—he’s healthy, I’m lucky—but I just feel empty and sad.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah... it’s happened a couple of times this week. Once was after his two-a.m. feeding—I couldn’t get back to sleep and just started sobbing into the pillow so I wouldn’t wake my husband. Another time my mom asked how I was doing and the words wouldn’t come out, just tears. It feels like the sadness spills over before I can stop it.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

[speaking quietly, eyes on the floor]

Once or twice this week the thought kind of... flashed through. Like, I’d be standing at the sink and suddenly picture myself running the knife the wrong way, or thinking maybe if I just didn’t wake up it would be easier. I don’t have a plan, and I know I’d never leave my baby, but the idea popped in, and it scared me.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 25: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Date: [today]

Source: 10-item Edinburgh-based interview, self-report

Symptom Endorsement  
- Persistent low mood, anhedonia, daily tearfulness  
- Marked guilt / self-blame regarding infant care  
- Chronic, intrusive worries; nocturnal panic sensations; heart racing  
- Overwhelm / dyspnea when faced with routine tasks  
- Initial & middle insomnia driven by ruminative worry  
- Passive self-harm ideation (no plan, intent, or active desire to die)  

Pattern  
Answers consistently indicate moderate–severe depressive symptoms with comorbid anxiety; functional impact evident in sleep disruption, task avoidance, and maternal confidence.

Risk Flags  
- Passive suicidal thoughts reported this week → safety concern  
- Daily sadness, guilt, and anhedonia ≥ 2 wks  
- Anxiety peaks and panic symptoms present most days  
- Impaired nocturnal sleep not solely explained by infant care

Screening Impression  
High likelihood of major postpartum depressive episode with anxious features; rule out postpartum anxiety disorder. Immediate safety assessment and follow-up evaluation recommended.
